Mobile networks, fibre, and IoT are not just digital infrastructure - they are also drivers of modern energy systems. They are key catalysts of energy access, and also drive energy planning and rollout at the largest scales. These synergies are only growing.

But the gaps are still huge. Around 2.2 billion people are not connected to the internet. Most of them in low- and middle-income countries. Synergies continue here, too. Many of the communities that most need energy access are also the least digitally connected. And, without reliable connectivity, digital tools for energy planning, monitoring, and payment simply cannot scale.

Connectivity anchors energy systems and amplifies their impact. And countries are leveraging this combined role through:

📡 Closer coordination between energy and connectivity providers, especially at the last mile
🛠️ ‘Dig Once’ and co-deployment approaches to roll out infrastructure faster and at lower cost
🌍 Exploring Community Networks in remote and underserved areas - bringing energy, connectivity, and local digital skills together

Connectivity is not a side issue in the energy transition. It is central to inclusion, resilience, and scale. Read more about the Digital Energy Stack here: https://lnkd.in/e7PebbrX

👉 We're very interested in hearing about other initiatives, interventions, and insights from countries and #energy stakeholders around the world. How can we support countries in shaping connectivity efforts for inclusive energy impact? Let us know in the comments!
